title: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Intelligent Personal Finance Management Systems
authors: D'Souza, M.; Bhegade, P.; Bhalekar, P.; Bhavsar, Y.
tldr: A comprehensive qualitative literature review surveys ML techniques across PFMS components including budgeting, forecasting, anomaly detection, group expense management, and explainable AI, identifying fragmentation and gaps in current research.
problem_and_motivation: Current PFMS research is scattered across isolated segments such as budgeting, expense forecasting, anomaly detection, and group expense management, preventing cohesive intelligent solutions. Existing systems rely on rigid rule-based logic lacking personalization, adaptability, and predictive insights. There is no comparative analysis across models to clarify their respective strengths and weaknesses for intelligent personal finance.
approach: Conducted a qualitative literature survey and comparative analysis of ML techniques across PFMS components.
Reviewed statistical methods including EWMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA for budgeting and forecasting.
Examined deep learning approaches such as LSTM and GRU for capturing long-term dependencies in expenditure sequences.
Analyzed unsupervised methods including Isolation Forest for spending anomaly detection in personal finance.
Evaluated hybrid and ensemble forecasting frameworks combining ARIMA and LSTM outputs.
Surveyed group expense management techniques including graph-based settlement optimization and ML-based payer prediction.
Provided a structured taxonomy of PFMS components with comparative insights across learning methods.
Discussed explainable AI considerations for anomaly detection and user trust in financial systems.
findings: Isolation Forest consistently achieves superior detection capability relative to density-based and boundary-based anomaly alternatives in PFMS contexts.
Hybrid ARIMA-LSTM ensemble formulations enhance forecast robustness across heterogeneous financial conditions compared to standalone models.
LSTM-based budgeting captures long-term dependencies while introducing challenges related to data dependency and interpretability.
Rule-based budgeting mechanisms assume consistent spending behavior and offer limited adaptability when patterns change.
Deep learning approaches for anomaly detection require large training data volumes and impose computational overhead limiting real-time mobile deployment.
Graph-based settlement optimization reduces total transactions required to settle group debts.
Explainable AI techniques including post-hoc interpretability and attention mechanisms are increasingly incorporated into PFMS anomaly pipelines.

definitions.definition: Personal Finance Management Systems, tools for tracking, analyzing, and controlling individual financial activities.
Exponentially Weighted Moving Average, a statistical technique assigning greater weight to recent observations.
Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms for long-term dependency modeling.
Explainable Artificial Intelligence, techniques providing human-readable explanations for ML model decisions.
Gated Recurrent Unit, a simplified recurrent architecture compared to LSTM with fewer parameters.
An unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm that isolates observations through recursive partitioning.
AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average, a statistical time-series forecasting model combining AR, differencing, and MA components.
Optical Character Recognition, technology for automatically extracting text from images such as receipts.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This review consolidates the fragmented landscape of ML techniques applied to personal finance management by surveying budgeting, forecasting, anomaly detection, group expense management, and explainable AI within a unified taxonomy. It provides qualitative comparative analysis across statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid approaches, highlighting trade-offs in interpretability, scalability, adaptability, and data requirements. The paper identifies critical research gaps including the lack of cohesive PFMS frameworks, insufficient cross-model comparisons, and unresolved challenges in explainability and user trust.
directly_justifies: Isolation Forest achieves superior anomaly detection capability relative to density-based alternatives in PFMS environments.
Hybrid ARIMA-LSTM formulations enhance forecast robustness by combining linear trend modeling with non-linear residual capture.
LSTM-based budgeting captures long-term temporal dependencies but requires substantial data and computational resources.
Current PFMS research is fragmented across isolated components without cohesive integration.
Explainable AI is increasingly needed to maintain user trust in learning-driven financial systems.
limits: Qualitative survey without quantitative performance benchmarks across techniques.
Does not address specific implementation or deployment considerations for mobile PFMS.
Synthesizes existing literature rather than proposing novel algorithms or architectures.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) received high relevance as the paper surveys current PFMS architectures and their limitations. Domains 6 and 7 (Predictive Modeling and Budgeting) received high relevance due to extensive coverage of forecasting algorithms and budgeting techniques. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) received high relevance for its treatment of Isolation Forest and related methods. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) received medium relevance for its discussion of spending pattern clustering. Domain 10 (Privacy) received medium relevance for identifying trust and privacy as open challenges. Domain 9 (Mobile Design) and Domain 12 (Evaluation) received low to medium relevance for mentioning deployment constraints and providing comparative frameworks. Domains 1-3, 11, 13, and 14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, expense categorization frameworks, engagement mechanisms, savings goals, or synthetic data generation.

limitations: Qualitative synthesis without empirical performance comparisons across techniques.
Does not address domain-specific challenges such as Filipino financial behaviors or local regulatory contexts.
Synthesizes existing literature rather than providing new empirical results or novel algorithmic contributions.
remember_this: The review provides a unified taxonomy of ML techniques across five PFMS components.
Isolation Forest consistently outperforms density-based methods for personal spending anomaly detection.
Hybrid ARIMA-LSTM forecasting combines linear and non-linear modeling for robust predictions.
Current PFMS literature is fragmented, with no single system integrating budgeting, forecasting, anomaly detection, and recommendations.
Explainable AI is identified as a critical requirement for user adoption of intelligent financial systems.
